subject: Vendor security kickoff — SIG prefill, evidence handoff & clarifying questions
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@finhealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@finhealth.com
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Kickoff: security assessment for Redwood integration

Hi Mina —

Thanks again for the demo today. We want to kick off the security questionnaire and start collecting evidence as we evaluate Redwood for a pilot. A few quick answers from our side to get you started:

- SOC 2: In progress (Type II audit scheduled for Q4 2027). We have SOC 2 Type I report from 2026.
- Data residency: Primary production in us-west-2; backups cross-region within US.
- Regulated data: We will potentially route PHI through Redwood for the pilot; HIPAA BAAs are required.

We prefer a SIG or CAIQ (SIG preferred if it will speed things up). Please send a prefill packet and let us know what evidence you typically provide for encryption key management and logging.

Can we schedule a 30-min kickoff tomorrow morning PST to align owners and timing?

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Ruiz
Director, Security & Privacy
FinHealth

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@finhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: security assessment for Redwood integration

Thanks Elena — really appreciate the quick context. A few clarifying questions before the call so we can pre-populate the SIG and map owners: 

1) SOC 2 timeline: you mentioned Type II in Q4 — would you be able to share the previous (Type I) scope or a redacted report? That helps us determine which controls we can reference vs. where we should collect fresh evidence.
2) PHI use case: can you confirm expected data flow (ingest -> processing -> storage) and whether PHI will be stored long-term or only transiently during inference?
3) Preferred questionnaire: sounds like SIG is fine — are there any custom questions your procurement/legal want added to the SIG?
4) Evidence owners: please list 1–2 technical owners (name + email) who can pull logs, config screenshots, or KMS attestations.
5) SSO / SAML: will you require SAML SSO in the pilot? If so, which IdP?

I attached our SIG prefill template and an evidence-mapping markdown that explains typical artifacts we provide (screenshots of console settings, artifact manifests for SOC2 controls, KMS policy snippets). If you prefer CAIQ instead we can pivot.

Proposed kickoff: Tue 10 Aug, 9:00–9:30am PST — confirm and I’ll send a calendar invite with an agenda.

Attachments: [redwood-sig-prefill-template.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)], [redwood-evidence-mapping.md (text/markdown)]

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Security Liaison, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0124

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@finhealth.com>

Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 00:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: security assessment for Redwood integration

On Mon, Aug 9, 2027 at 4:04 PM Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks Elena — really appreciate the quick context. A few clarifying questions before the call so we can pre-populate the SIG and map owners: 
>
> 1) SOC 2 timeline: you mentioned Type II in Q4 — would you be able to share the previous (Type I) scope or a redacted report? That helps us determine which controls we can reference vs. where we should collect fresh evidence.
> 2) PHI use case: can you confirm expected data flow (ingest -> processing -> storage) and whether PHI will be stored long-term or only transiently during inference?
> 3) Preferred questionnaire: sounds like SIG is fine — are there any custom questions your procurement/legal want added to the SIG?
> 4) Evidence owners: please list 1–2 technical owners (name + email) who can pull logs, config screenshots, or KMS attestations.
> 5) SSO / SAML: will you require SAML SSO in the pilot? If so, which IdP?

Hi Mina — thanks, answers inline below.

1) SOC 2: we can share a redacted Type I report by end of day (redacted to remove customer names). I’ll post it to the shared Drive link and give you access.
2) PHI flow: ingest (FinHealth ingests PHI), call RW inference inferences (transient cache) -> results returned to our systems. We do not intend to persist PHI inside Redwood beyond request processing for the pilot; long-term storage will remain in our environment.
3) SIG vs CAIQ: procurement prefers SIG (they use the SIG as canonical control mapping) but legal may add 3-4 custom clauses — nothing blocking for kickoff.
4) Evidence owners: security@finhealth.com (operational owner) and Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@finhealth.com> (platform engineer) — both can pull logs and provide screenshots.
5) SSO: yes — Okta as IdP; pilot will not require SAML initially but may later.

I’ve uploaded the redacted Type I to the Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aB2cPrefillSample

See you tomorrow at 9am PST.

—
Elena Ruiz
Director, Security & Privacy, FinHealth

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@finhealth.com>, security@finhealth.com
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: security assessment for Redwood integration

Looping in a quick note from infra side before the call:

- For encryption evidence we typically provide KMS key policy snippets, envelope encryption flow diagrams, and a public KMS attestation report for dedicated deployments. If FinHealth needs HSM-backed keys or a customer-managed key (CMK) workflow, flag that now — it affects rollout timeline.
- Also, can you confirm the subnet / VPC expectations and whether traffic must stay within us-west-2? We can stage a private deployment in the same region for the pilot if required.

I’ll bring the sample artifacts to the kickoff and map them to SIG control IDs so procurement sees exactly where each artifact addresses a control.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
